composing_text: Division troops landed at Red Beach this day. The northern attack at Tulagi was a separate landing the same morning.
source_locator: R2225: ch. III; R2226: ch. III
notes: Opening landing of the Guadalcanal campaign. Vandegrift commanded the landing force ashore. Confidence 0.7: Miller ch. III and Zimmerman ch. III both date the Guadalcanal landing to 7 August 1942 at the Red Beach / Lunga area.

source_locator: R2225: ch. IV, Action on the Ilu River; R2226: ch. IV, Battle of the Tenaru
current_activity: defending the eastern perimeter at the Ilu
notes: The 21 August 1942 battle was fought on the Ilu River, immediately east of the Lunga perimeter. Miller titles it “Action on the Ilu River”; Zimmerman and many American accounts call it the Battle of the Tenaru. The place used is the Ilu (PL4904), not the Tenaru River proper (PL4905). Confidence 0.7: both official histories date the battle to 21 August.

source_locator: R2225: ch. V, The Counteroffensive, 12-14 September; R2226: ch. V, The Battle of the Ridge
current_activity: defending Bloody Ridge south of the airfield
notes: Battle of Edson’s / Bloody Ridge, 12–14 September 1942. The dated row is 13 September, the main night of the attack, at the ridge (PL4908). Confidence 0.7: Miller and Zimmerman agree on the dates and the place.

location_qualifier: Lunga perimeter; command passed to Patch
source_locator: R2225: ch. IX; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9
current_activity: handing over command ashore and beginning evacuation
notes: On 9 December 1942 Major General Alexander M. Patch relieved General Vandegrift in command of troops ashore, and evacuation of the 1st Marine Division began: the 5th Marines sailed that day (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). Miller states that by the end of December the rest of the division had followed. This row is the command change and the start of the withdrawal, not a claim that the entire division left on 9 December. Confidence 0.7: Army and Marine official histories agree on the date.
